# Places

## Sable Pond

Forty acres, spring fed, a mile inland and eighty feet above the harbor. Freezes
solid by the second week of January in a good year. The grid is marked with a horse
plow and cut with saws; the channel runs downhill to the pond house door.

## The pond house

Stone below, planked above, sixty feet by forty. Ice stacked in courses and packed
in sawdust from the shingle mill. Two doors: the water door on the pond side, the
wagon door on the road side. It holds four thousand tons when it is full, and it has
been full twice since 1918.

## The scale house

One room and a stove at the wagon door. The platform scale, the tally book, the
nails on the wall where the route slips hang. Odile's whole territory.

## The harbor

A mile down the hill. The cannery wharf, the coal shed, the fish house, the town
landing. Schooners load ice from the wagon at the wharf, not from the pond.

## The road

Dirt from the pond down to the harbor, dirt again for eleven miles to the county
seat. Mud season closes the second road entirely from late March to early May.
